{
 "summary": "This change routes `-addnode` startup configuration options through `CConnman::AddNode` instead of directly appending them to the added-node list, warning on duplicates. It also improves duplicate detection in `CConnman::AddNode` by checking hostname and effective port pairs, recognizing that hostnames with and without an explicit default port refer to the same destination.",
 "problem": "When the same peer is specified multiple times via `-addnode` configuration arguments, or specified with and without its default port, all entries are stored in the added-node list. While disconnected, the connection thread attempts to resolve and connect to each duplicate entry on every retry cycle, producing redundant DNS lookups, connection attempts, and log spam.",
 "evidence": [
  "Author description: 'Both entries are currently stored. While the destination is disconnected, ThreadOpenAddedConnections() processes each entry during every retry cycle. This can cause redundant DNS lookups, connection attempts, and log messages. getaddednodeinfo also reports the repeated entry.'",
  "Commit beadf6a96d: 'CConnman::AddNode rejects equivalent numeric addresses, but compares unresolved hostnames as raw strings. As a result, the same hostname with and without an explicit default port can be stored twice.'"
 ],

<category name="p2p" title="P2P">
## Covers

Everything between this node and other nodes: connection management and
peer selection, address management, the message protocol and its
transport (including the encrypted v2 transport), block and transaction
relay including compact blocks, headers sync, transaction request and
orphan handling, network-level DoS protections, and the Tor, I2P, and
CJDNS integrations. The P2P and Private Broadcast labels are a strong
prior.

Not p2p: what the node does with a block or transaction once received
(validation, mempool); RPCs that merely report peer state (rpc).

## What matters here

Resistance to attack first: eclipse and partition resistance, DoS
resistance in message handling and resource accounting, and privacy of
transaction origin. Then relay correctness and liveness: blocks and
transactions propagate reliably and quickly, and nothing gets stuck.
Then interoperability with the rest of the network and with new
protocol features (BIPs) that other software depends on. Then bandwidth
and resource use, which node operators feel. Then connectivity across
network types and platforms.

Protocol changes with a specification and other implementations
waiting rank higher than local optimizations. Refactors count when they
retire a known hazard in message handling.
